messages:
inc-bot: ALERT: High tail latency and elevated 5xx rate for /generate (model: redwood-7b) in us-west-2. p95 -> 2300ms, 5xx -> 9% over last 2m. Pager: #eng-oncall
Alice (oncall): paging in. seeing the alert, pulling up dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/abcd/continuous-batching
Bob (runtime): I see queue depth on batcher nodes spiking, microbatch size distribution skewed. p50 microbatch=16, p95=128, max=1024. weird
Carla (eng-sre): any KV cache errors? memory churn?
Bob (runtime): yes - KV cache eviction rate jumped, OOM churn in kvcache-shard-3. logs:
```
kvcache[mem]: eviction_count=1.2M, insert_rate=9.4k/s, avg_kv_size=14kb
batcher: assembled_microbatch=1024, total_tokens=1.2M
```
Dan (infra): that insert_rate looks like a cache blowup. what's the traffic source? any big prompt storms?
Alice (oncall): customers reporting slow interactive responses (chat apps), CS ticket #INC-2042 from Acme reporting timeouts
Eve (support): Confirming - Acme shows many timeouts and retry loops, they see p99 ~ 9s
Bob (runtime): hypothesis: continuous batching combined with long prefixes and correlated request bursts created super-large microbatches. the runtime then allocates KV cache entries for many queries causing memory pressure and cascading eviction; as eviction increases, subsequent requests take longer (cache-miss penalty) -> perf cliff.
Carla (eng-sre): agreed. mitigation plan options:
  1) reduce max_microbatch and enforce jitter
  2) temporarily disable continuous batching for affected model pool
  3) clear KV cache shards to stop churn
  4) route high concurrency customers to dedicated pool
Alice (oncall): executing 1 & 3 first. Dan can you approve cache eviction? need to avoid losing warm prefixes for other customers but we need stability.
Dan (infra): approve. run safe-evict on shard-3 and shard-5 with throttle
Bob (runtime): running commands:
```
redwoodctl runtime config set --pool=us-west-2 --model=redwood-7b --max_microbatch=8 --microbatch_jitter_ms=25
redwoodctl kvcache safe-evict --shard=3 --rate=500/s
redwoodctl kvcache safe-evict --shard=5 --rate=500/s
```
Alice (oncall): applied. Patching rollout id r/8243 to disable continuous batching for the model as emergency fallback:
```
redwoodctl rollout create --desc="emerg-disable-continuous-batching" --match=model:redwood-7b --patch='{"continuous_batching":false}' --priority=high
```
Carla (eng-sre): good. I'm watching mem and p95.
(30s)
inc-bot: NOTE: rollout r/8243 started, targeting 12 nodes. progress: 25%
Bob (runtime): early signal: p95 from 2300ms -> 540ms, 5xx -> 1.2% . KV eviction rate dropping.
Eve (support): Acme confirms partial improvement, still some retries but better
Alice (oncall): continuing: scaling warm pool + routing high concurrency IPs to dedicated fallback
Dan (infra): scaling dedicated pool: +8 GPUs in us-west-2, routing rule applied for client Acme IPs
Bob (runtime): after full rollout p95 stabilized ~ 210ms, 5xx ~0.4%, microbatch max back to ~16
Carla (eng-sre): recording incident ticket INC-2042. tagging for postmortem. Actions taken:
- reduced max_microbatch -> 8
- set microbatch_jitter_ms -> 25
- safe-evicted kvcache shards 3 & 5
- emergency rollout to disable continuous batching for redwood-7b
- scaled dedicated fallback pool and routed impacted clients
Alice (oncall): handing off to night shift @Bob (runtime) in 20m. Bob can you pick up follow-up and verify no regression on canary traffic?
Bob (runtime): yes will monitor for 4h and follow up with small perf test harness. I'll also push guard: automatic throttle to refuse building microbatches > 128 tokens or > 64 requests.
Carla (eng-sre): add alert: new rule to page if microbatch_size > 256 for >1m or kvcache eviction_rate > 200k/min. we'll add it to infra runbook.
Eve (support): Notifying Acme SREs that mitigation is in place. also offering a post-incident recap
Alice (oncall): ack. creating follow-up ticket: ENG-5791 (root cause analysis & long-term fix: better batching heuristics, per-customer rate envelopes, and KV cache admission control)
Dan (infra): FYI: we're also enabling controlled jitter at ingress LB to reduce client correlation
inc-bot: Incident INC-2042 acknowledged by Alice, status: mitigation in progress
Bob (runtime): putting a checklist in the ticket with commands and rollback steps
Alice (oncall): thanks team. If anyone sees p95 > 500ms re-pager. Otherwise I'll close this thread after handoff.
(2h later)
Bob (runtime): no regression observed in the 2h window. KV eviction rate normal. leaving monitoring on. will post datapoints to the ticket tomorrow.
Carla (eng-sre): assigning postmortem owner Alice/ENG-5791. please include timeline and customer impact numbers.
Eve (support): Acme happy with support response; no SLA credit requested yet. closing loop tomorrow.
Alice (oncall): handing off: Bob (runtime) now primary, Carla (eng-sre) secondary.
